messages:
fran: Heads-up — ran into a nasty onboarding footgun. Sample-app ships with a checked-in .env containing REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, while my shell has REDWOOD_ORG_KEY. The SDK sent both headers and the gateway returned `conflicting_auth` mid-stream; the client restarted and I lost conversation state.

oliver: That's rough. Which SDK and version? Did it send Authorization + X-Redwood-Project?

fran: Node SDK v2.9.1. Logs: 

```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer org_live_foo",
  "X-Redwood-Project-Key": "proj_live_bar"
}
Response: 401 {"error":"conflicting_auth","detail":"multiple tokens present"}
Stream: client reconnect -> user-visible restart
```

pat: We need a three-part fix: 1) sample-app should not COPY .env in Dockerfile and include .env.example instead; 2) SDK should implement a canonical AuthResolver with deterministic precedence and single-header enforcement; 3) streaming recovery: implement onAuthRefresh hook to swap tokens in-flight and resume rather than full tear-down.

oliver: For precedence, propose: explicit param > CLI flag > ORG env (REDWOOD_ORG_KEY) > PROJECT env (REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY) unless REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true > sidecar/netrc > legacy files. Defaulting org above project avoids CI surprises.

fran: I like the override flag idea. Also suggest SDK emit a dev-only `WARN` at startup if multiple auth sources are detected, showing which source won and pointing to docs. Rate-limit to once per minute so logs don't drown. Example: `WARN devex auth: multiple auth sources detected; using REDWOOD_ORG_KEY (exported in shell). Run with --auth-source to override. https://redwood.dev/auth-precedence`

pat: Good. Implementation checklist for SDK teams:
- Add AuthSource enum + precedence table in docs
- Add `--auth-source` CLI override and SDK param to pin source
- On startup, detect multiple sources -> WARN once (rate-limited) and include X-Auth-Resolved header in DEV builds only
- Ensure SDK never sends multiple auth headers; if both present, pick winner and drop the other
- For streaming 401: call onAuthRefresh hook -> replace header -> retry frames; only close if refresh fails

oliver: Also handle rotation: if we get 403/401 and the auth source was cache/netrc, invalidate cache and re-resolve once before failing. Add clear actionable error message if re-resolve fails.

fran: I'll open two small PRs: one to change the sample-app Dockerfile and add .env.example, another with a tiny SDK patch for the startup warning and debug header. Will include repro steps and sanitized logs.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: staging build 2026-03-21_12:10 succeeded (2.4.3)

pat: Thanks — ping @dev-tools on the PRs. We should also add a short snippet to the onboarding guide about common auth pitfalls (checked-in .env, sidecars, CI env injection).

fran: Will do. Thanks everyone.
